neighbours.label: ' at' right after a reporting verb, introducing the event where something was said or announced ('said at a news conference')
fire: The new budget targets are realistic, the minister said at a press briefing on Monday.
Details of the merger were announced at a shareholders meeting in Zurich.
We will not raise prices this year, the chief executive told reporters at the trade fair.
The plan was unveiled at a conference on renewable energy.
Our goal is full employment, the governor said at a rally in Ohio.
The findings were presented at the annual meeting of the society.
Talks will resume next week, a spokesman said at a briefing in Geneva.
The senator declared at a town hall that she would run again.
quiet: The new budget targets are realistic, and the office opens at nine on Monday.
Details of the merger were filed with regulators in Zurich.
We will not raise prices this year, so tickets stay at ten dollars.
The plan was drawn up by engineers working on renewable energy.
Our goal is full employment, and the factory sits at the edge of town.
The findings were published in the annual journal of the society.
Talks will resume next week, after the holiday in Geneva.
The senator arrived at the airport late on Thursday.

notes: ' at' is 24 of the top 32 peaks, nearly all 'said/disclosed at <event>'. Near misses keep ' at' in non-reporting contexts (location, time, price), testing the context rather than the word.
